title: Second reason: what a rational creature needs to reach its natural end, knowing and loving God, is natural
source_text: LIII. Praeterea creaturae rationali non corruptae naturale est id sine quo naturalem suum finem assequi nequit. Sed finis creaturae rationalis est, ut Deum agnoscat, amet atque colat. Ad hoc fuit enim a Deo condita. Hunc finem autem assequi non potest, si absque justitia & sanctitate creetur; Et si consideretur ut destituta donis illis quae per Adami peccatum amisimus.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover to a rational creature not corrupted that is natural without which it cannot attain its natural end. But the end of a rational creature is that it acknowledge, love and worship God. For to this it was founded by God. But it cannot attain this end, if it be created without justice and sanctity; And if it be considered as destitute of those gifts which we lost through Adam's sin.
pass_b_english: Further, what an uncorrupted rational creature needs in order to reach its natural end is natural to it. The end of a rational creature is to know, love and worship God, for that is what God made it for.
It cannot reach that end if it is created without righteousness and holiness, that is, if it is thought of as stripped of the gifts we lost through Adam's sin.

choices.english: that is, if it is thought of
choices.why: The printed sentence 'Et si consideretur ...' is a fragment continuing the condition; the English joins it to the preceding clause as an explanation.
rejected: And even if it is considered
